definitions.explanation: To become elderly or advanced in years. Often used for people and animals.
Figuratively, when something loses its vitality or freshness.

examples.english: My parents have also grown old.

examples.japanese: {老|お}いても{元気|げんき}でいたい。
examples.english: I want to stay healthy even when I grow old.

examples.japanese: {老|お}いた{犬|いぬ}が{日向|ひなた}ぼっこをしている。
{人|ひと}は{誰|だれ}でも{老|お}いていく。
{祖母|そぼ}は{老|お}いてもなお、{毎日|まいにち}{散歩|さんぽ}を{続|つづ}けている。
examples.english: Even in her old age, my grandmother continues her daily walks.

examples.japanese: {建物|たてもの}が{老|お}いて、あちこちに{傷|いた}みが{見|み}える。
examples.english: The building has aged, and damage can be seen here and there.

examples.japanese: {老|お}いた{町|まち}に{新|あたら}しい{風|かぜ}を{吹|ふ}き{込|こ}みたい。
examples.english: I want to breathe new life into this aging town.

examples.japanese: この{会社|かいしゃ}は{組織|そしき}が{老|お}いてきている。
examples.english: This company's organization is becoming worn and outdated.

examples.japanese: {文化|ぶんか}が{老|お}いて、{新|あたら}しいものが{生|う}まれなくなった。
examples.english: The culture has grown stale and stopped producing anything new.

notes:
{老|お}いる is an intransitive verb ({自動詞|じどうし}). It is classified as an ichidan verb but has some irregular features from classical Japanese. There is no transitive pair.

ASPECT ({ている}):
{老|お}いている indicates an ongoing or resulting state of being old.

CONJUGATION:
- {老|お}いる (dictionary form)
- {老|お}いて (te-form)
- {老|お}いた (past)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {老|お}いてもなお - even in old age
- {老|お}いた{親|おや} - aged parents
- {年|とし}を{取|と}って{老|お}いる - to grow old with age

LITERARY NOTE:
This verb has a somewhat literary or formal feel. In everyday speech, {年|とし}を{取|と}る is more commonly used to express aging.
